overal.goal: Review and plan bringing better-ccflare's main features into boof (the 'Owlish' part): users add accounts of different kinds (Claude, ChatGPT and others) and boof uses them to run its agents, choosing and rotating accounts and pausing agents to spend wisely. Boof may run Claude Code or other harnesses under the hood, but pick a harness that boof can control itself. Start with research: what better-ccflare does (accounts, load balancing, rate-limit handling, usage), and which agent harnesses boof can drive and steer programmatically (Claude Agent SDK, Codex, OpenCode, others), with a recommendation. Output: a design document, then a plan.
overal.stack: TypeScript monorepo (Node 22 / Bun), Hono server, React + Vite UI (shadcn/ui on Tailwind v4), vitest

rules.do: Read README.md, docs/boof-runner.md and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-ui-redesign-design.md before changing code.
Write a failing test first, then make it pass; keep the change focused on this goal.
Run `npm run typecheck && npx vitest run && npm run build:server` before finishing.
Every new capability is reachable through REST, MCP and the CLI as well as the web UI and the desktop app.
Write the research and the design to docs/superpowers/specs/ before any code.
rules.dont: Do not change public API or MCP shapes without updating docs and the OpenAPI document.
Do not commit secrets, data roots or build output.
Do not store account credentials in plain text; use the existing secrets approach or propose one in the design.

versions.version: Requested by the owner on 2026-10-29; not started.

D2 (owner, 2026-10-29): integrate better-ccflare rather than rebuild it — boof controls it and applies the spend rules. Check the legal side first (better-ccflare's licence and what it allows when bundling, integrating or calling it) and credit it by name (better-ccflare) in the docs and the UI where it is used. Harness: choose the best solution (roadmap recommends adding a Claude Agent SDK adapter as the controllable default and keeping the CLI adapters); record the reasoning in the design.

tests.strategy: Design review with the owner first; then unit tests for account selection and pause rules, and an end-to-end run with the mock tool.
